choices_the_plan_left_open: Passing a fixed bar (route 3): a method passes a bar when its episode-mean deletion area on the complete-case population is at or below the bar. The method with the largest share of calls at or below the bar uses call-level shares within the complete-case population.

Ties: when several methods share the highest mean in one bootstrap draw, the probability_best credit for that draw is split equally among them. An exact tie in the means leaves the preferred method undetermined and is reported as a tie. A route that compares an undetermined preferred method is reported as undetermined, not as a change.
Replication banks (B1, S and each Month 8 stratum) report the seven primary contrasts with descriptive 95% intervals and no multiplicity claim.

Coverage: before unblinding, the coverage simulation is repeated at the realized complete-case episode counts, with a literal two-point outlier scenario (point masses at 0.1 and -3.0, 5% at -3.0) added beside the existing normal-mixture rare-extreme scenario. Every reported interval states the simulated coverage of its method at its episode count, or that no simulation exists at that count.
corrections_to_follow_the_plan_as_writte: Descriptive intervals are 95% percentile intervals: every method, fixed order and z-scaled advantage, and every difference outside the unique test. The level 0.05/4 is used only for the best-minus-second interval of the unique test, and 0.05/7 only for the seven primary contrasts on the primary bank.

The complete-case rule is applied as written. For each modality and direction, an episode enters a comparison only when every planned call has a defined area and a defined random-order reference for every ranking in the comparison, under both Q and N. Calls the collector planned but never reached count as planned calls and exclude their episode. Each excluded episode is reported with its reason.

Route 4 compares the preferred method on the complete-case population with the preferred method on all available calls. On all available calls, each method is averaged over its own defined calls, with episodes weighted equally.

The amendment-1 extreme count is the number of episodes with any call of the compared quantity below -1. It is reported for each primary contrast, for each method's advantage and for the best-minus-second difference.
BCa and t intervals accompany the best-minus-second intervals as well as the primary contrasts (amendment 1).

The round-rule sensitivity is computed from the stored responses, so no new forwards are needed. The max1_round and round schedules differ only where round gives zero groups, and the zero-group response is the curve's first value.
The nominal-axis area is reported beside the realized-fraction area. RMS is reported as its raw area in action units.

Numerics comparisons are reported against two labelled references and a reference is never compared with itself:
  - the fp32 A2 T512 map, on every fp32 context;
  - the A4 map, on the contexts where A4 converged.
On the A4 subset, the qualification test (A4, GL128 and A2 T512 within relative L1 1e-3 pairwise) and the resolution floor (largest pairwise disagreement) are computed.
Numerics summaries are given for the plan's populations: the Month 8 strata pooled (all available Month 8 contexts) and the new P bank, with per-bank detail beside them.
reason: An independent review of the analysis code against the plan, before any production outcome was read, found places where the code departed from the plan and places where the plan left a choice open. The code is corrected to the plan, and the open choices are fixed here before the analysis runs.
unchanged: Methods, controls, responses, metrics, primary family, multiplicity rule, decision rule, bootstrap (draws, seed, resampling of episodes) and populations.
